newsitem.title: UK: Europe may solve UK one-engine cargo jet ban-Flight.
newsitem.headline: Europe may solve UK one-engine cargo jet ban-Flight.

text.p: The UK Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) concedes that night operations of single-engined commercial cargo aircraft could be accepted under new European regulations, 'Flight' reports in its June 25 issue.
The proviso is that these flights avoid built-up areas, the magazine said.
It added that the CAA concession came despite the authority's own recent legal victory upholding a ban on such flights in UK airspace.
A European joint aviation requirements study group is tackling the subject of single-engine planes using "sparsely populated corridors" for night flights, 'Flight' quotes the CAA as saying.
The study group,which is due to convene within the next three months, would have to agree on a system requiring aircraft to avoid overflying built-up areas, said the magazine.

It added that the potential compromise had come to light as the CAA won a court case preventing a UK company, Martini Airfreight Services, using a Norwegian-registered Cessna Caravan 208B for night newspaper delivery flights.
